# `plot.skyscapeR.sigTest()` {#fn-plot-skyscaper-sigtest}

W01 checked clipped local intervals, the pointwise envelope and the global probability label against the stored fit. [W01 results](w01-plot-geometry.qmd).

**Verified on 2.0.9006.** On a full-turn panel, a cluster crossing north can have two visible segments with one shared probability. [S03 rerun](s03-scoring-checks.qmd).

**Validation on 2.0.9005.** The tested public fits plotted the stored local interval midpoints and significance symbols. North-crossing intervals can appear separately. [S03 results](s03-scoring-checks.qmd).

[Function index](function-index.html#idx-plot-skyscaper-sigtest)

```{=html}
<p>The observed curve and envelope use the azimuth or declination grid stored in the test
result. The two-tailed display shades between its lower and upper pointwise bounds; the
one-tailed display shades up to the upper bound from zero. Optional annotations show the
stored global p-value and the local intervals, coloured by deficit or excess and
labelled by p-value symbols. The observed and envelope curves jointly set the visible vertical range. The lower panel identifies adjusted and legacy unadjusted local results. The plot reads the fitted result without repeating the
simulations. New local values use maximum-cluster adjustment under the complete null;
cluster endpoints remain descriptive, not confidence limits. Legacy fits retain their
original unadjusted values. Interpret local regions alongside the whole-curve test.
</p>
```

**Interpretation and limits.** Keep the numerical global and adjusted local p-values with the output. Symbol thresholds and the placement of a band on the plot do not supply extra precision about its endpoints.
